Something went wrong while submitting the form. 2-METHYLISOBORNEOL (MIB) 2-Methylisoborneol is an irregular monoterpene that, together with geosmin, is the source of most of the taste and odor outbreaks in drinking water with biological origins. ABSORPTION SPECTRUM A material’s absorption spectrum is the fraction of electromagnetic radiation that it absorbs over a range of wavelengths. The absorption spectrum depends on the atomic and molecular structure, composition, and interactions within the material. ABUNDANT CYANOBACTERIAL SPECIES The most abundant cyanobacteria include Prochlorococcus, the predominant marine cyanobacteria; Synechococcus is also a marine species. Freshwater cyanobacteria include several species of Microcystis, Dolichospermum sp., Anabaena sp., and Aphanizomenon sp., among others. AEROBIC RESPIRATION Aerobic respiration releases chemical energy in cells to power their activities. This process relies on a series of metabolic reactions involving molecular oxygen to convert the nutrients’ chemical energy into energy in the form of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and then release carbon dioxide and water as waste products. Respiration is a catabolic process that breaks large molecules into smaller ones, releasing energy by replacing the weak high-energy bonds in molecular oxygen with stronger bonds in the resulting products. AEROSOLS An aerosol is a suspension of fine solid and/or liquid particles suspended in the air. Aerosols can be natural, such as sea salt particles, dust, pollen, or many others, or human-made, like ammonium sulfate particles and soot from anthropogenic emissions. Aerosols are classified into two types: primary particles, which are emitted directly into the atmosphere, and secondary aerosols, which form in the air from precursor gases. Aerosol particles play a crucial role in cloud formation by acting as condensation nuclei around which cloud droplets materialize, making them key players in the climate system. ALGAL BLOOM An algal bloom occurs when an algae population in an aquatic system grows rapidly, often manifested as water discoloration from the algal pigments. Algal blooms are usually caused by eutrophication, i.e., excess nutrients that are released into the water body. Algal blooms can contribute positively to or have harmful effects on the aquatic ecosystem. For example, the algae can serve as food for organisms in higher trophic levels, their high density in the upper water layer can block the sunlight, or they can secret toxins into the water. ALGICIDE/ALGAECIDE An algaecide is a substance intended to mitigate and control harmful algae. Algaecides are often used to destroy harmful algal blooms (HABs). However, algaecides may be dangerous in large quantities but are often required to produce effective results. BlueGreen Water Technologies develops safe, effective, and environmentally friendly algaecides to mitigate HABs and restore natural ecosystems. ALUMINIUM SULFATE Aluminum sulfate is a salt with the chemical formula Al₂(SO₄)₃, mainly used as a coagulating agent for water treatment and purification. ANABAENA SP. Anabaena is a genus of nitrogen-fixing filamentous cyanobacteria found in shallow waters and moist soil. Anabaena may form blooms during the summer, producing neurotoxins that endanger local animals and human health. ANABAENOPSIS SP. Anabaenopsis is a genus of filamentous cyanobacteria capable of producing microcystins that are toxic to both humans and animals. ANAEROBIC RESPIRATION Anaerobic respiration uses an electron acceptor other than molecular oxygen (O2). Anaerobic organisms use fewer oxidizing substances than oxygen, such as nitrate and sulfate, therefore releasing less energy per oxidized molecule. For this reason, anaerobic respiration is less efficient than aerobic respiration. ANATOXIN-A Anatoxin-A is an acute cyanotoxin, also known as the Very Fast Death Factor (VFDF), because it can be lethal within minutes to hours for numerous animals, especially cattle and dogs. Anatoxin-A is found in a number of cyanobacteria, including Anabaena, Aphanizomenon, Microcystis, Planktothrix, Oscillatoria, and Cylindrospermum. APHANIZOMENON SP. Aphanizomenon is a genus of cyanobacteria that inhabits freshwater lakes and can cause harmful blooms by producing various cyanotoxins. AQUATIC ECOSYSTEM An aquatic ecosystem includes communities of organisms within and around a water body. Every water body is a unique ecosystem that constantly changes over time (day and season). ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) Artificial intelligence (AI) is a branch of computer science focused on developing computers or computer-controlled machines to perform tasks that require human intelligence. BACTERIAL COLONY A bacterial colony is a visible mass of bacteria originating from a single mother cell, therefore containing genetically identical bacteria (clones). jobs.title: Carbon capture
jobs.description: Net Zero Go Beyond Net Zero with Net Blue™ Science-led carbon and water ecosystem restoration Go Beyond Net Zero with Net Blue™. Science-led carbon and water ecosystem restoration Net Blue™ is BlueGreen’s integrated approach to freshwater ecosystem restoration and carbon mitigation, developed in alignment with the Social Carbon Foundation methodology and currently undergoing certification validation. Net Blue™ combines harmful algal bloom remediation with monitored carbon dynamics in eutrophic freshwater systems. By restoring ecosystem balance, improving water quality, and supporting biodiversity recovery, Net Blue™ enables the generation of carbon credits based on measured and verified environmental outcomes. Contact us Our Mission: Restoring Freshwater Ecosystems BlueGreen Water Technologies was founded to address the global challenge of freshwater degradation caused by eutrophication and harmful algal blooms. Our technologies are designed to restore ecological balance in impacted water bodies by targeting cyanobacteria and algae that disrupt aquatic systems. These interventions aim to improve water quality, support ecosystem recovery, and enable healthier outcomes for communities, wildlife, and surrounding economies. Learn more From Water Restoration to Carbon System Impact Net Blue™ interventions are designed to influence carbon dynamics in freshwater ecosystems through the restoration of ecological balance in eutrophic systems. Following treatment, changes in organic matter cycling, algal biomass dynamics, and sedimentation processes may contribute to measurable carbon outcomes, subject to MRV verification. Large freshwater systems contain significant carbon reservoirs, and interventions are assessed for their potential impact within defined carbon accounting boundaries. Carbon credit revenue may support broader environmental and community water restoration initiatives where applicable. ‍ *Net Blue™ considers biodiversity and ecosystem integrity as co-benefits aligned with emerging global nature-positive frameworks, including post-COP15 biodiversity objectives. Learn more The Net Blue™ Advantage No Residue or Footprint Biodegradable formulations are designed to break down naturally without leaving harmful residues in the water. Requires no infastructure Deployed directly in affected water bodies without the need for permanent infrastructure. Cost effective Designed to leverage carbon revenue streams to support scalable ecosystem restoration. Scalable Applicable across freshwater systems of varying sizes, subject to site-specific assessment. Added value May contribute to both carbon sequestration and methane mitigation, subject to verification. Monitoring, Reporting & Verification (MRV) BlueGreen’s Net Blue™ framework incorporates environmental monitoring and data collection processes designed to support transparent project evaluation and carbon quantification. Project monitoring may include: - satellite and remote sensing analysis - field sampling - water quality measurements - biomass assessment - sediment analysis - ongoing ecological monitoring BlueGreen is advancing methodologies intended to align with leading carbon market standards and independent verification requirements. Verified Outcomes Project outcomes are assessed through structured monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) processes in accordance with applicable carbon methodology frameworks. Carbon credit issuance is subject to independent verification and regulatory approval prior to market release. Learn more Interested in finding out more about NetBlue’s credits? Contact us How a Net Blue™ PCredit is Generated 1 Site Identification: Identify a suitable freshwater system through scientific assessment and eligibility screening. 2 Stakeholder & Regulatory Engagement: Engage relevant authorities and secure required permits and approvals. 3 Treatment Implementation: Execute the approved ecological intervention and treatment plan. 4 Monitoring & Data Collection: Gather environmental data throughout treatment and post-treatment phases. 5 Independent Verification: Validate outcomes under an approved Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) framework 6 Credit Issuance: Issue and register verified carbon credits for market distribution. Services About Home Water Treatment Formulations BlueGreen’s innovative Lake Guard® formulations are designed to successfully remediate cyanobacteria and harmful algal blooms and improve water quality in lakes of any size worldwide. Because no two water bodies are alike, we develop customized treatment strategies for each site, leveraging our proprietary AI systems to best target the infestation. Our plans are optimized to produce highly effective results, rehabilitating ecosystems, wildlife, and aquatic species while using the least amount of product necessary and minimizing waste. BlueGreen Lake Guard® water remedies have been proven many times over in locations around the globe. Advantages of Lake Guard® Products Simple The ready-to-use floating and dissolving formulations self-distribute to the target locations (via wind and current).​ Efficient Minimal quantities are needed to achieve maximal impact. Safe* NSF/ANSI/CAN 60 certified and US EPA* registered. Scalable Can remediate and/or improve water clarity in water bodies of all sizes, from ponds to large lakes. Effective Measurable results within 24 hours after treatment. Applies to Lake Guard® Blue and Oxy formulations Lake Guard® OXY The unique Lake Guard® Oxy mode of action triggers oxidative stress in cyanobacterial populations, prompting cell death among the cyanobacteria. Its active ingredient, sodium percarbonate, releases hydrogen peroxide (a substance that has long been used as a safe algaecide) when it comes into contact with water. The clean Lake Guard® Oxy process breaks the granular active ingredient down into simple water and oxygen, causing no harm to the environment. Lake Guard® Oxy’s special biodegradable coating enables the product to float on the water’s surface, traveling to the affected locations where it releases its active ingredient. Safety data Product label CONTACT US Lake Guard® BLUE The active ingredient in Lake Guard® Blue is copper sulfate, which has long been used around the world as a safe and effective algaecide. Lake Guard® Blue causes oxidative stress and severe damage to algal and cyanobacterial populations. The product interrupts their photosynthesis by binding to their enzymes. Lake Guard® Blue’s special biodegradable coating enables the product to float on the surface of the water, traveling to the affected locations where it releases its active ingredient. Safety data PRODUCT LABEL Lake Guard® DEW The active ingredient in Lake Guard® Dew is aluminum sulfate, which has long been used as a safe and effective water treatment. Lake Guard® Dew is encapsulated in a thin, inert, biodegradable coating, allowing it to disperse throughout the water. It works as a coagulant, causing particles to clump together into clusters for easy removal. In this way, Lake Guard® Dew rapidly and dramatically improves water clarity. Holistic services and products can resolve pervasive global water problems, both present and future.​​ EXPERTISE TO TARGET ANY CHALLENGE Treating water bodies of all shapes and sizes BlueGreen provides solutions, services, and products for water bodies of all dimensions, from the smallest ponds to the largest lakes, seas, and oceans. Treating harmful algal blooms Our team of scientists offers customized solutions for any HAB-infested water body. We draw insights into a lake’s issues by applying our artificial intelligence to the lake’s parameters and infestation data. This enables us to prescribe the best Lake Guard® formulation for the objectives at hand: to treat algal infestations, prevent future outbreaks, or enhance water clarity. BlueGreen scientists use AI algorithms to optimize the treatment plan, producing highly effective results with minimum product usage. Remote satellite- and drone-based monitoring BlueGreen Water Technologies uses satellites and drones to assess and monitor large expanses of water from afar. We track the presence and progression of algal blooms using digital RGB (red, green, blue) images and infrared sensors to measure substance concentrations in the water. We convert these indicators into a bloom status, which defines the bloom locations, intensity, and dispersion. This data drives strategic decisions on how and where to apply treatment. Water Scientist Consultations Leading BlueGreen experts provide advisory services to help you respond rapidly to emergency situations, regain control, and avert disaster. BlueGreen scientists also offer strategic and tactical recommendations in non-urgent cases and preventive care. Customized Reports Keeping your finger on the pulse of your water health is key to controlling looms. We generate detailed, targeted reports on the cyanobacteria and algal bloom conditions in water bodies being monitored or treated, including treatment progress and bloom progression. Net Blue™ (Carbon Capture and Sequestration credits) Rising CO2 levels in the atmosphere cause climate change and threaten life on the planet. Cyanobacteria play an essential role in reducing atmospheric CO2 by naturally bio-mineralizing carbon. BlueGreen treatments mimic bio-mineralization at scale, removing large amounts of CO2 from the air to bring down carbon levels. BlueGreen cyanobacteria remediation and carbon sequestration generate Net Blue™ carbon credits – Super Credits approved by Social Carbon®, an international standard for nature-based solutions. Lake Guard® Monitor In-water sensing service for remote condition monitoring. Monitor and protect your water bodies with our annual subscription service offered in collaboration with AquaRealTime. Water probes collect and transmit vital intelligence to your personalized online dashboard in real time. View blue-green algae status, turbidity, temperature, sunlight, wind, rain, and more – to make informed decisions about water care. Working together to keep your water bodies safe 1 Initial Contact Reach out to us by phone, email, or online form to discuss your water concerns. 2 IDENTIFICATION & ANALYSIS A BlueGreen representative will help assess your specific situation and requirements. We will outline our approach, and together, we will determine the best course of action. 3 Site Evaluation We assign a lead water scientist and a project manager to your case. Field personnel, supported remotely by our research scientists, visit your site and conduct field research to fine-tune the treatment method. 4 Remediation Your lead water scientist and project manager develop the precise treatment protocol based on your needs. You perform the remediation or request that BlueGreen conduct it.​ 5 EVALUATION & FUTURE PROJECTS​ We evaluate the remediation program’s success and use data collected to determine future water treatment and prevention plans.​ Follow us STAY UP TO DATE!
